title: Goal sprint cartography — two-week check & micrometrics
content:
Purpose: a lightweight, context-rich two-week sprint map for personal OKRs. This is a working scratchpad — quick to iterate, cheap to change.

High-level objective (Q2 alignment): Improve developer-facing product guidance so that experimental teams can ship with predictable inference cost and latency. This is my personal contribution thread that connects to team OKR: reduce median inference latency across top-5 workloads by 12% and lower costs of small-batch requests by 8%.

Why this sprint: narrow focus on three complementary levers I can influence this sprint: 1) prompt templates & guardrails for caching, 2) quick eval harness to measure tail latencies on representative prompts, 3) micro-optimizations in the local dev runbook to reduce iteration time.

Top-level success metrics (two-week targets):
- Signal A: Weekly validated prompt templates that increase prefix-hit rate to >= 25% on the test harness (baseline ~12%).
- Signal B: Median dev-run iteration time (local infra + mock service) reduced from 28s -> 20s for the targeted workflow.
- Signal C: One regression test in the eval harness showing tail latency (95th pct) improvement >= 10% on at least 2 prompt families.

Measurement plan:
- Where measured: local dev harness (dev-machine), lightweight benchmarking harness in /tmp/eval-small, telemetry snapshots exported to a CSV I own.
- How often: daily micro-snapshot (end of day) + full experiment run every Wed & Sun.
- Quick acceptance: if daily moving average shows >= 10% improvement on metric, mark as yellow/green.

Micro-actions (day by day plan):
- Day 1 (Mon): baseline snapshot; confirm data ingestion into personal CSV; create two prompt template variants (cache-friendly, minimalid).
- Day 2: implement prefix tagging helper (10–15m) + run 3 warmup reps; note failures.
- Day 3: quick A/B harness: route 50% of requests through template A, 50% B; collect prefix-hit and latency.
- Day 4: triage errors; refine guardrails; capture notes for team sync.
- Day 5: consolidate wins; prepare short slide for Friday async update (2 slides).
- Day 6–7: weekend full eval; deep-dive tails.
- Day 8–10: iterate on runbook, push small scripts to my fork, open one PR.
- Day 11–12: partner with Lina on validation; finalize metrics and write short retro note.

Check-in template (what I update each day):
- Date / DOW
- Quick context (one line)
- Delta vs baseline (numbers)
- Blockers (if any)
- Next 24 hours

Experiment catalog (short):
- EXP-001: Cache-friendly templates (A/B). Hypothesis: stricter prefix structure increases KV cache reuse for common assistant scaffolds. Measure: prefix-hit rate, per-token latency. 
- EXP-002: Local dev warmup stitching (process-level cache reuse). Hypothesis: persistent local runtimes reduce first-request cold-start. Measure: median cold vs warmed latencies.
- EXP-003: Minimal generation mode (token budget heuristics). Hypothesis: short-circuiting early returns reduces cost while preserving quality for template-driven outputs. Measure: token counts, human QA pass rate (quick sample).

Quality checks & gating:
- If EXP-001 increases prefix-hit but degrades human-evaluated quality on >10% of sampled outputs, stop and revisit prompt design.
- If median iteration time < 20s but end-to-end test fails in more than 2 flows, hold PR.

Risks / open questions (notes-to-self):
- Does a higher prefix-hit rate imply real user-perceived improvement or just micro-bench artifacts? Need small user-facing sample test.
- Potential coupling with service-side batching — local gains may not translate to hosted. Flag for later analysis.
- Timebox: avoid deep infra refactors this sprint. Focus on small, reversible changes.

Retro template (end of two weeks):
- What worked: list 3 things that moved the metric.
- What didn’t: 3 blockers or surprises.
- Quick wins to carry forward: 3 items.
- Escalations / ask list: who I need to pull in next (SRE, infra, Lina for quality).

Contingency rules (if/then):
- If after 7 days no measurable prefix-hit improvement, pivot to warming strategies (EXP-002).
- If a change causes >5% regression in median quality sample, revert to last known-good template and open a postmortem note.

Calendar mapping (where this lives in my week):
- Mon: 45 min focused block (EOD snapshot)
- Wed: 60 min deep-run + sync note to Rafi
- Fri: 20 min async slide + team update
- Sun: full run + retro drafting

Energy & context log: (short)
- Note: this sprint I’m low on deep-focus mornings (calendar overloaded). Prioritize EOD snapshots and batch noisy tasks to afternoons.

Notes to self (unresolved):
- Draft a one-paragraph explainer for why prefix-friendly templates are a low-risk first step for customers. Keep short for product slack.
- Tie EXP-001 to a customer scenario (dedicated vs hosted differences) — makes measurement more meaningful.

Next steps (immediate):
1) create EXP-001 A/B variants and run baseline (today).
2) push runbook update to my fork with a one-line summary for reviewers.
3) add quick Slack note to #eng-serving-runtime with preliminary plan and ask if anyone has canned prompt examples to reuse.

Quick log (live):
- 2026-03-01 Mon: Baseline taken; prefix-hit 11.8%, median local iteration 28s.
- 2026-03-02 Tue: Implemented prefix tag helper; test run shows prefix-hit 15.4% (warm), iteration 26s; small JSON error on template B.
- 2026-03-04 Thu: A/B run started, data flowing to CSV; noticed unexpected tokenization differences for whitespace-heavy examples.

Scratch area (short ideas):
- Could we expose a "cache hint" scalar in the SDK: low/medium/high — easier for product teams to opt-in.
- Add a quick QA probe that samples 10 outputs and runs a paraphrase-similarity check to ensure no semantic drift when templates change.

End of doc: keep this lightweight. Delete or fork when it becomes actionable PRs.

---
Metadata note: will convert to a more formal personal retro doc if wins are consistent across two cycles.
